body: Give reasons for each cooking precaution: (i) adding lemon juice to fresh fish; (ii) whisking eggs over a bowl of warm water; (iii) proofing dough in bread making. Also list **four** types of flour used in cookery.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(i) Lemon juice on fish:** reduces/neutralises the **fishy odour** (acid reacts with amines); **firms/whitens** the flesh; adds **flavour**; slightly **preserves**/slows bacterial growth.
>
> **(ii) Whisking eggs over warm water:** gentle heat helps the eggs **trap more air** and gain volume faster; makes the foam **more stable**; dissolves sugar quickly; prevents the eggs from **curdling/cooking**, as direct heat would.
>
> **(iii) Proofing dough:** allows the **yeast to ferment** and produce CO₂ so the dough **rises**; gives a **light, open texture**; develops **flavour**; relaxes gluten for shaping.
>
> **Types of flour:** plain (all-purpose), self-raising, wholemeal (wholewheat), strong (bread) flour, cassava flour, maize/corn flour, rice flour.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Each precaution has a chemical or physical reason; state it clearly.

## Simplified explanation

Lemon = odour and firmness; warm water = volume; proofing = rising.

body: (a) State **three** functions of vitamin D. (b) List **six** sources of calcium. (c) State **four** deficiency conditions of calcium.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Vitamin D: (1) promotes **absorption of calcium and phosphorus** from the gut; (2) helps the **formation and hardening of bones and teeth**; (3) maintains normal blood calcium for **nerve and muscle** function; (4) supports immunity.
>
> **(b)** Calcium sources: **milk**, cheese, yoghurt, **small fish eaten with bones** (sardines, anchovies/*keta school boys*), **dark-green leafy vegetables** (kontomire), beans/soya, eggs, fortified cereals, okra.
>
> **(c)** Deficiency: **rickets** (children), **osteomalacia** (adults), **osteoporosis**, **tetany**/muscle cramps, poor/decaying teeth, delayed blood clotting, stunted growth.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Vitamin D and calcium work together.

## Simplified explanation

D absorbs calcium; milk and fish bones; rickets.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.

body: (a) State **three** effects of **cooking** on fruits. (b) State **two** instances when fruits need to be cooked. (c) Enumerate **five** rules to follow when cooking fruits.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Cooking (1) **softens** the fruit (cellulose softens, pectin dissolves); (2) **destroys vitamin C** (heat- and water-soluble); (3) changes **colour and flavour**; (4) kills micro-organisms; (5) **sugar dissolves** into the fruit/syrup.
>
> **(b)** When fruit is **unripe, hard or sour** (e.g. green mango, cooking apples, plantain); for **preservation** (jam, marmalade); for **variety** in dishes (stewed fruit, pies, sauces); for invalids/infants who need soft food.
>
> **(c)** Wash before peeling/cutting; use **little water**; cook for the **shortest time**, gently (simmer); **cover** the pan; prepare **just before cooking**; use non-reactive (stainless/enamel) pans; serve soon after cooking; add sugar at the right time (late, to keep the shape).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Minimise vitamin C loss: little water, short time, covered pan.

## Simplified explanation

Softens, loses vitamin C; cook unripe fruit; little water, short time.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.

body: (a) Name **two** classes of vegetables, with **two** examples each. (b) State **three** changes that occur when vegetables are cooked. (c) State **three** rules to obtain maximum nutrients from cooked vegetables.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Leafy: **cabbage, kontomire, lettuce, spinach**; Roots/tubers: **carrot, yam, cassava, cocoyam**; Fruits: **tomato, garden egg, okra, pepper**; Bulbs: **onion, garlic**; Pulses: **beans, peas**; Stems: celery; Flowers: cauliflower, broccoli.
>
> **(b)** **Softening** (cellulose softens, starch gelatinises); **loss of water-soluble vitamins** (C and B) and minerals into the water; **colour changes** (green → olive in acid/overcooking); **flavour** changes; reduction in bulk; destruction of micro-organisms.
>
> **(c)** Wash **before** cutting; cut **just before cooking**; use **little water** and add vegetables to **boiling** water; cook for the **shortest time** with the lid on; don't add soda; **use the cooking water** in soups/sauces; serve immediately.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Water-soluble vitamins are the main loss.

## Simplified explanation

Leafy and root; softening and vitamin loss; little water, short time.

body: (a) State **five** points to consider when selecting utensils for cooking. (b) State **five** factors that determine the size of a family kitchen.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** **Purpose**/suitability for the task; **material** (heat conduction, non-reactive); **durability** and quality of construction; **ease of cleaning**; **size** for the family; **cost**/budget; **weight and handling** (insulated handles, well-fitting lids); type of **cooker/fuel**; storage space; safety.
>
> **(b)** **Size of the family**; **income**/cost of building; **size of the house/plot**; **activities** carried out there (eating, laundry); amount and type of **equipment**; **type of cooking/fuel**; entertainment and lifestyle; number of people working in it at once.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Answer with short, clear points.

## Simplified explanation

Purpose, material, durability, cleaning, cost; family size, income, space.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.

body: (a) State **five** factors to consider when determining the quality of **canned** foods. (b) State **three** advantages and **two** disadvantages of a **supermarket**.
answer:
> [!answer]
> **(a)** Check the **expiry/best-before date**; can must not be **dented, rusted, bulging (blown) or leaking**; **label** intact, with ingredients, manufacturer and batch number; **brand reputation**/approval (FDA/GSA); on opening, no **off-smell, spurting or discoloration**; price relative to weight/content.
>
> **(b)** **Advantages:** a **variety** of goods under one roof; **self-service**, saving time; **fixed, labelled prices** (no haggling); clean, hygienic environment; items often in good condition with proper storage; card payments.
>
> **Disadvantages:** **impulse buying**; prices often **higher**; no bargaining; may be far from homes; little personal attention; long queues at peak times.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

A blown can signals dangerous bacterial growth (botulism).

## Simplified explanation

Date, can condition, label; variety, self-service vs impulse buying, cost.
hint: Give the points with a brief explanation each.
